correctness.rationale: For every a>0 and c!=0, the first-coordinate multiplier exceeds 1, preserving sign and bounding increments of y away from zero. This gives a quadratic denominator, an absolutely convergent logarithmic product for a finite nonzero X, Cesaro y_n/n->cX, and an exact telescoping tail X-x_n. The bootstrap yields X-x_n=a/(c^2 X n)+O(log n/n^2), followed by an absolutely summable centered y increment proving its logarithmic term and finite constant C. All signs and zero-axis boundary cases were checked, including c<0 and x0<0. The 384018 finite checks support but do not prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: The originating model is explicitly proposed to exhibit a line of fixed points and diverse competing compact attractors in other parameter regimes. The global fate of nonfixed real initial data in the positive rational-coefficient regime is a natural dynamical gap: every trajectory leaves compact subsets in a ballistic coordinate while its transverse coordinate saturates. The exact universal signed logarithmic shear and n^-1 saturation coefficient classify slow approach to the escape velocity; the dyadic finite-difference limit is observable without the unknown additive phase. This is a whole-plane structural classification rather than an arbitrary sample, numerical increment, or textbook stability check, although techniques are elementary and the opposite-sign conditional escape has related terms.
